acqinfo.head: Acquisition Information
acqinfo.p: These records were transferred to the Library of Virginia from Giles County (Va.) as part of an undated accession.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: Giles County Petitions for Re-Enslavement were originally described as part of the Giles County (Va.) Free and Enslaved Records, 1817-1864, but were removed to the present Giles County (Va.) Petitions for Re-Enslavement, 1860, record to enhance discoverability in September 2026.

These records have been processed, scanned, and indexed by E. Woodward, L. Neuroth, and LVA staff for the purposes of digitizing them for the digital project Virginia Untold: The African American Narrative.

bioghist.head: Historical Information
bioghist.p: Context for Record Type: Petitions for Re-enslavement consist of petitions of free Black individuals choosing to be re-enslaved. An act passed by the Virginia General Assembly in 1806 required formerly enslaved people to leave the commonwealth within twelve months of being granted their freedom. Individuals were forced to leave behind family, friends, and community who remained enslaved. In addition, many emancipated people did not have the financial means or social support to move to a free state. One option to preserve family and relationships was to return to slavery. In 1856, the Virginia legislature passed an act allowing free Black individuals who desired to remain in the commonwealth to petition for re-enslavement. Only a small number of free Black Virginians petitioned the courts to re-enslave themselves to an enslaver of choice, and an even smaller percentage succeeded. Many petitioners chose enslavers they knew well or who owned a spouse or family member. These petitions include the petitioner's name, previous enslaver, means of emancipation, and new desired enslaver.

Locality History: Giles County was named for William Branch Giles, United States senator from Virginia in 1806 when the county was created from Montgomery, Monroe (now in West Virginia), and Tazewell Counties. Several subsequent additions were made from Wythe (1808), Monroe in 1829 and Mercer in 1841 (both now in West Virginia), Craig (1880), and Tazewell (1826 and 1836) Counties. The county seat is Pearisburg.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content
scopecontent.p: Giles County (Va.) Petitions for Re-Enslavement, 1860, include a petition in which Martha Brown asked to be enslaved to William W. McComas. The court granted her request, citing their belief "that there is no fraud or collusion between [Brown and McComas] but that the application of the said Martha Brown is made in good faith."
